vitamin d3 (cholecalciferol)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Vitamin D3 is a fat-soluble vitamin commonly added to foods and supplements to support calcium absorption and bone health. It is generally safe, but excessive intake can lead to toxicity.","details":"Because it is fat-soluble, Vitamin D3 can accumulate in the body, and very high supplemental doses over time may cause hypercalcemia (too much calcium in the blood), leading to nausea, kidney stones, or kidney damage. Risk depends heavily on dose and total intake from all sources (supplements plus fortified foods); staying within established upper intake limits reduces concern. Some Vitamin D3 is sourced from lanolin (sheep wool) or fish oil, which may matter for dietary preferences, but this is not a general safety risk.","category":"Vitamin (fat-soluble)"}

vitamin b12 (cobalamin)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Vitamin B12 (cobalamin)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Vitamin B12 is a water-soluble vitamin used in fortified foods and supplements to support red blood cell formation and nervous system function. It is generally considered safe at typical and even relatively high supplemental amounts.","details":"As a water-soluble vitamin, excess B12 is usually excreted in urine, and toxicity is rare for most people. Some individuals may experience mild side effects (such as acne-like skin reactions or gastrointestinal discomfort) at higher doses, but serious adverse effects are uncommon. Absorption can be reduced in people with certain conditions or medications (for example, metformin or acid-reducing drugs), which is more relevant to effectiveness than safety.","category":"Vitamin (water-soluble)"}

yellow 6 (sunset yellow fcf)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Yellow 6 (sunset Yellow Fcf)","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Yellow 6 is a synthetic food dye used to add orange-yellow color to foods and supplements. Most people tolerate it, but it can be a concern for those sensitive to certain artificial colors.","details":"Yellow 6 is approved for use in many countries, but some individuals report sensitivity reactions such as hives or worsened hyperactivity-like symptoms in susceptible children. It provides no nutritional benefit and is mainly used for appearance, so reducing intake may be preferable if you are sensitive to artificial dyes.","category":"Artificial color (synthetic dye)"}

blue 1 (brilliant blue fcf)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Blue 1 (brilliant Blue Fcf)","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Blue 1 is a synthetic food dye used to create blue or green shades in foods and supplements. It is generally considered safe at regulated levels but may bother dye-sensitive individuals.","details":"Blue 1 is widely permitted and typically used in small amounts, yet some people may experience intolerance-type reactions (for example, skin symptoms) or prefer to avoid it due to being an artificial color. It does not add nutritional value and is included primarily for visual appeal.","category":"Artificial color (synthetic dye)"}

turmeric oleoresin (color)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Turmeric Oleoresin (color)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Turmeric oleoresin is a natural coloring derived from turmeric that provides a yellow-orange hue. It is generally well tolerated in food and supplement products.","details":"This color extract contains curcuminoids and related compounds that give turmeric its characteristic color, and it is commonly used as a natural alternative to synthetic dyes. In higher supplemental amounts turmeric extracts can cause mild digestive upset in some people, but the amounts used for coloring are typically small.","category":"Natural color (plant extract)"}

thiamin mononitrate (vitamin b1)__food__.analysis: {"name":"Thiamin Mononitrate (vitamin B1)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Thiamin mononitrate is a stable form of vitamin B1 used to fortify foods and supplements. It is generally safe at typical dietary and supplement amounts.","details":"Vitamin B1 supports energy metabolism and normal nerve function, and deficiency is more common than toxicity. Adverse effects are rare because thiamin is water-soluble and excess is typically excreted, though very high supplemental doses may cause mild gastrointestinal upset in some people. People with certain medical conditions or on specific medications should follow clinician guidance for high-dose use.","category":"Vitamin / Fortificant"}

riboflavin (vitamin b2)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Riboflavin (vitamin B2)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Riboflavin is an essential B vitamin added to foods and supplements to support normal energy metabolism. It is generally safe at typical dietary and supplement amounts.","details":"Riboflavin helps the body convert carbohydrates, fats, and proteins into energy and supports skin, eye, and nervous system health. Excess riboflavin is water-soluble and is typically excreted in urine, which can cause harmless bright-yellow urine. Very high supplemental doses may occasionally cause mild stomach upset, but serious toxicity is rare.","category":"Vitamin"}

folic acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Folic Acid","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Folic acid is the synthetic form of folate (vitamin B9) used in fortified foods and supplements. It is beneficial for preventing neural tube defects, but excessive intake can be a concern for some people.","details":"High supplemental intake may mask vitamin B12 deficiency by correcting anemia while neurological damage progresses, which is why some populations should avoid chronically high doses unless medically supervised. People with certain genetic variants (such as MTHFR) may prefer natural folate forms (e.g., 5-MTHF), though folic acid remains effective for most individuals. Staying within recommended daily amounts from supplements and fortified foods helps minimize risk.","category":"Vitamin / Fortificant"}

rice__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Rice","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Rice is a common grain used as a carbohydrate base in many foods. It is generally safe for most people when consumed as part of a balanced diet.","details":"Rice provides mostly starch with small amounts of protein and minimal fat. Brown rice offers more fiber and micronutrients than white rice, but both can fit into a healthy diet. Rice products can contribute to higher glycemic impact, especially when refined, and trace arsenic can be a consideration with frequent high intake, particularly in rice-based foods.","category":"Grain / Carbohydrate"}

sugar__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sugar","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Sugar adds sweetness but increases added-sugar intake, which can negatively affect metabolic and dental health when consumed in excess. Occasional intake is generally fine, but frequent high consumption is a concern.","details":"High added-sugar diets are associated with weight gain, higher triglycerides, increased risk of insulin resistance, and dental cavities. Sugar provides calories without meaningful vitamins, minerals, or fiber, making it easy to overconsume. If sugar is listed near the beginning of the ingredient list or appears in multiple forms, the product may be relatively high in added sugars.","category":"Added Sweetener"}

canola and/or soybean oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Canola And/or Soybean Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Canola and soybean oils are common vegetable oils used for cooking and food processing. They are generally considered safe for the general population; soybean is a common allergen but still low risk for most people.","details":"These oils are typically high in unsaturated fats and are widely used in packaged foods for texture and shelf stability. Highly refined soybean oil contains little to no soy protein, which reduces allergen exposure for many people with soy allergy, though sensitive individuals should still use caution. As with any added fat, overall quantity matters, and frequent intake of ultra-processed foods using refined oils can displace more nutrient-dense foods.","category":"Vegetable Oil / Fat"}

salt__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Salt","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Salt is a common seasoning and preservative, but it can significantly increase a product's sodium content. Excess sodium intake is linked to higher blood pressure in many people.","details":"Salt provides sodium, which is essential for fluid balance and nerve function, but most diets already contain more than recommended. Regularly consuming high-sodium foods can increase the risk of hypertension and cardiovascular disease, especially in salt-sensitive individuals. People with high blood pressure, kidney disease, or heart failure are often advised to limit sodium.","category":"Seasoning / Sodium source"}

red 40__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Red 40","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Red 40 is a synthetic food dye used to add red color to foods and beverages. Some people may be sensitive to it, with potential behavioral or allergy-like reactions.","details":"Red 40 (Allura Red AC) is approved for use in many countries, but it is sometimes associated with increased hyperactivity symptoms in susceptible children and with intolerance reactions in a small subset of individuals. Rarely, it may trigger hives or other pseudoallergic responses, particularly in people with sensitivities to food dyes. It adds no nutritional value and is mainly included for appearance.","category":"Artificial colorant"}

yellow 5__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Yellow 5","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Yellow 5 is a synthetic dye used to create yellow coloring in foods and supplements. It can cause sensitivity reactions in a small number of people.","details":"Yellow 5 (Tartrazine) is a widely used artificial colorant and must be declared on labels in some regions due to sensitivity concerns. A small subset of individuals may experience hives, asthma-like symptoms, or other intolerance reactions, and it has also been studied in relation to hyperactivity in susceptible children. Like other artificial colors, it provides no nutritional benefit and is primarily cosmetic.","category":"Artificial colorant"}

zinc oxide__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Zinc Oxide","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Zinc oxide is a mineral form of zinc used to fortify foods and supplements. It can help meet zinc needs, but excessive intake may cause adverse effects and this form may be less well absorbed than some other zinc salts.","details":"Zinc supports immune function, wound healing, and normal taste and smell, and zinc oxide is sometimes used because it is stable. Compared with forms like zinc citrate or zinc gluconate, zinc oxide can be less bioavailable, so some products use higher amounts to compensate. High total zinc intake (especially from multiple supplements) can cause nausea and, over time, contribute to copper deficiency and immune or lipid changes.","category":"Mineral (Zinc Source)"}

vitamin a palmitate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Vitamin a Palmitate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Vitamin A palmitate is a fat-soluble form of vitamin A used in fortified foods and supplements. It is beneficial at appropriate doses but has a higher toxicity risk than water-soluble vitamins if overconsumed.","details":"Vitamin A is important for vision, immune function, and skin and mucosal health, and palmitate is a common, stable supplemental form. Because it is fat-soluble, it can accumulate in the body, so combining multiple products containing preformed vitamin A can increase the risk of excess. High intakes over time may lead to liver strain and other symptoms, and pregnancy requires particular caution with high supplemental preformed vitamin A.","category":"Vitamin (Fat-Soluble)"}

pyridoxine hydrochloride (vitamin b6)__f.analysis: {"name":"Pyridoxine Hydrochloride (vitamin B6)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Pyridoxine hydrochloride is a common supplemental form of vitamin B6 used to support normal metabolism and nervous system function. It is generally safe at typical fortification and supplement levels.","details":"Vitamin B6 plays a role in amino acid metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, and red blood cell function, and pyridoxine HCl is widely used due to stability. Most people tolerate it well, especially at amounts near daily needs. Very high long-term supplemental doses can cause sensory nerve symptoms, so total intake matters if multiple B6-containing supplements are used.","category":"Vitamin (Water-Soluble)"}

bht (butylated hydroxytoluene) sodium as.analysis: {"name":"Bht (butylated Hydroxytoluene); Sodium Ascorbate; Ascorbic Acid (vitamin C)","riskLevel":"high","summary":"This line includes a synthetic preservative (BHT) plus Vitamin C forms used for antioxidant support and to help prevent oxidation in the product. For most people, Vitamin C ingredients are low concern, while BHT is the main potential issue.","details":"BHT is an antioxidant preservative used to slow rancidity and maintain freshness, but it is a more controversial additive and some people prefer to limit it due to mixed evidence and sensitivity concerns. Sodium ascorbate and ascorbic acid are common Vitamin C forms that also act as antioxidants in foods; typical amounts are generally well tolerated. Very high Vitamin C intake can cause stomach upset or diarrhea in some individuals, especially when combined with other Vitamin C sources.","category":"Preservative and vitamins/antioxidants"}

niacinamide (vitamin b3)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Niacinamide (vitamin B3)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Niacinamide is a common form of Vitamin B3 used to support normal energy metabolism and overall nutrient status. It is generally well tolerated at typical food and supplement levels.","details":"Niacinamide is less likely to cause the flushing associated with nicotinic acid (another form of B3). At very high supplemental doses, it may cause nausea, headaches, or liver-related concerns, but these effects are uncommon at standard fortification or multivitamin amounts. People with liver disease or who take high-dose B3 supplements should be more cautious about total daily intake.","category":"Vitamin"}

reduced iron__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Reduced Iron","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Reduced iron is an iron fortificant used to help prevent iron deficiency. It can be beneficial for people with low iron intake, but excess iron may be a concern for some individuals.","details":"Reduced iron is commonly added to cereals and other fortified foods; its absorption can be lower than some other iron forms, but it still contributes to total iron intake. Too much iron can cause gastrointestinal upset (constipation, nausea) and may be harmful for people with iron overload conditions (such as hemochromatosis) or for young children if accidentally overconsumed. If you already take iron supplements or have high iron stores, monitoring total intake from all sources is advisable.","category":"Mineral (iron fortification)"}

monosodium glutamate (msg)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Monosodium Glutamate (msg)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"MSG is a flavor enhancer that adds savory (umami) taste and is generally considered safe at typical dietary amounts. Some people report sensitivity symptoms after large amounts, but evidence is inconsistent.","details":"MSG is the sodium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid naturally present in many foods, and it is used to boost flavor. In sensitive individuals, high intakes may be associated with short-lived symptoms such as headache or flushing, though controlled studies do not consistently confirm a cause-and-effect relationship. It also contributes sodium, which can matter for people limiting sodium intake.","category":"Flavor enhancer / Food additive"}

artificial and natural flavors__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Artificial And Natural Flavors","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Artificial and natural flavors are mixtures used to create or enhance taste, but their exact components are often not disclosed on labels. They are generally used in small amounts, yet can be problematic for people sensitive to certain flavor chemicals or carriers.","details":"These flavor blends may include solvents, carriers, and numerous aroma compounds; “natural” refers to the source, not necessarily a health advantage. Because formulas are proprietary, it can be hard to identify specific triggers for those with sensitivities (for example, certain aroma chemicals) or dietary restrictions. Occasionally, flavor systems may be derived from allergenic sources, but labeling rules vary and cross-contact is possible.","category":"Flavoring / Food additive"}

maltodextrin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Maltodextrin","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Maltodextrin is a processed carbohydrate used as a filler, thickener, or to improve texture. It is generally safe, but it can rapidly raise blood sugar in some people.","details":"Maltodextrin has a high glycemic index, so it may be a concern for people with diabetes, insulin resistance, or those aiming to limit blood-sugar spikes. In large amounts it can contribute extra calories with little nutritional value and may cause digestive discomfort (gas or bloating) in sensitive individuals. It is often made from corn, rice, potato, or wheat; highly refined forms typically contain minimal protein, but those with severe allergies should still use caution.","category":"Carbohydrate additive (filler/thickener)"}

citric acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Citric Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Citric acid is a common acidulant used to add tartness and help preserve freshness. It is widely considered safe at typical food and beverage levels.","details":"It helps control pH, enhance flavor, and can improve stability of products, especially drinks and gummies. In some people, frequent exposure in acidic foods may irritate the mouth or stomach, and regular intake of very acidic products can contribute to dental enamel erosion. Citric acid is often produced by fermentation (commonly using Aspergillus niger), but reactions are uncommon.","category":"Acidulant (preservative/flavoring)"}

potato__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Potato","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Potato is a whole-food starch that provides carbohydrates and some potassium and vitamin C. Health impact depends largely on processing method and portion size.","details":"Potatoes are naturally low in fat and contain fiber, but frying or heavy salting can reduce their overall nutritional quality. For people managing blood sugar, potato-based products can raise blood glucose quickly due to a relatively high glycemic impact.","category":"Vegetable / Starch"}

vegetable oil (palm and/or soybean and/o.analysis: {"name":"Vegetable Oil (palm And/or Soybean And/or Canola Oil)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"This is a blend of refined cooking oils used for frying and texture. Palm oil is higher in saturated fat, while soybean and canola oils are higher in unsaturated fats.","details":"Refined oils can contribute significant calories and may be repeatedly heated in snack processing, which can increase oxidation byproducts. Palm oil’s higher saturated fat content may be a concern for frequent, high intake, while soybean oil is a common allergen source but is generally safe for the population at large.","category":"Added Fat / Cooking Oil"}

seasoning__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Seasoning","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Seasoning is a catch-all term that can include salt, spices, flavorings, and additives. The main general concern is often high sodium and potential flavor enhancers.","details":"Without specifics, seasoning may contain ingredients like monosodium glutamate (MSG), yeast extract, artificial flavors, sugar, or anti-caking agents. If the product is a salty snack, seasoning can meaningfully increase sodium intake, which may be a concern for people monitoring blood pressure.","category":"Flavoring / Additive Mix"}

hydrolyzed soybean protein__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Hydrolyzed Soybean Protein","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A soy-derived protein broken into smaller peptides to improve solubility and taste. It is a common allergen (soy), but for the general population it is considered low risk.","details":"Hydrolyzed soybean protein is used to boost protein content and can also enhance savory flavor due to naturally occurring free amino acids. It may contain small amounts of naturally occurring glutamates from protein breakdown, which is not the same as added MSG. People with soy allergy should avoid it, but it is generally safe in typical food amounts.","category":"Protein ingredient"}

chili pepper extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Chili Pepper Extract","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"A concentrated extract used for heat and flavor, typically containing capsaicinoids. It can irritate the digestive tract in sensitive individuals, especially at higher doses.","details":"Chili pepper extract may trigger heartburn, stomach upset, or diarrhea in people prone to reflux or gastrointestinal sensitivity. Concentrated extracts can also cause a burning sensation in the mouth and throat, and may worsen symptoms of gastritis or ulcers. In normal culinary amounts it is usually well tolerated, but sensitivity varies widely.","category":"Flavoring extract"}

soybean oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soybean Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A common vegetable oil used for cooking and texture. It is a common allergen source (soy), but for the general population it is considered low risk.","details":"Soybean oil is primarily a source of fats, including polyunsaturated omega-6 fatty acids, and it is commonly used in processed foods. Highly refined soybean oil typically contains very little soy protein, which is the main allergen, though extremely sensitive individuals may still react. From a wellness perspective, overall dietary balance matters more than small amounts in a single product.","category":"Edible oil"}

disodium inosinate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Disodium Inosinate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Disodium inosinate is a flavor enhancer that boosts savory (umami) taste, often used alongside MSG. It is generally considered safe at typical food-use levels but may be a concern for certain sensitive individuals.","details":"It is a sodium salt of inosinate (a nucleotide) used to intensify flavor, especially in snacks, soups, and seasoning blends. People with gout or high uric acid may choose to limit large intakes of purine-related compounds, and those sensitive to flavor enhancers sometimes report symptoms. It also adds a small amount of sodium, which can matter in very salty foods.","category":"Flavor enhancer"}

disodium guanylate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Disodium Guanylate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Disodium guanylate is a flavor enhancer that increases umami intensity, commonly paired with disodium inosinate and/or MSG. It is generally safe in normal amounts but may not be ideal for everyone.","details":"This additive is a sodium salt of guanylate (a nucleotide) used to make foods taste richer without adding much protein or fat. Individuals managing gout or elevated uric acid sometimes limit high overall purine sources, and some people report sensitivity to flavor enhancers. Like other disodium additives, it can contribute a small amount of sodium to the product.","category":"Flavor enhancer"}

tbhq (preservative)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tbhq (preservative)","riskLevel":"high","summary":"TBHQ (tert-butylhydroquinone) is an antioxidant preservative used to prevent fats and oils from going rancid. It is approved for use in many countries within strict limits, but some consumers prefer to avoid it.","details":"TBHQ helps extend shelf life in processed foods by slowing oxidation, especially in products containing vegetable oils. At regulated levels it is generally considered safe, though high exposures in studies have raised concerns and a small number of people may experience sensitivity-like reactions. Its presence often indicates a highly processed food with added fats/oils.","category":"Preservative (antioxidant)"}

onion powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Onion Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Onion powder is a dehydrated onion seasoning used for flavor. It is generally safe for most people when consumed in typical food amounts.","details":"It adds onion flavor without adding much fat and only small amounts of sugars and sodium unless part of a salty blend. Some people with sensitive digestion (e.g., IBS) may experience gas or bloating because onions are high in fructans. It can also cause irritation for individuals with an onion intolerance, but this is not a common population-wide safety concern.","category":"Spice / Flavoring"}

sodium bicarbonate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sodium Bicarbonate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) is used as a leavening agent and acidity regulator. It is generally safe in foods at regulated, typical use levels.","details":"It contributes sodium, which can matter for people limiting sodium intake for blood pressure or kidney-related reasons, especially if many sodium-containing additives are present. In larger supplemental doses it can cause gastrointestinal upset and affect acid-base balance, but food-level amounts are usually small. If the product tastes noticeably salty or is a high-serving-size supplement, the total sodium per serving is worth checking.","category":"Leavening Agent / Acidity Regulator"}

red 40 lake__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Red 40 Lake","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Red 40 Lake is a synthetic food colorant (a lake form of Allura Red) used to color foods and supplements. It is approved for use, but some people prefer to limit artificial colors.","details":"A small subset of individuals may experience sensitivity reactions (e.g., hives or worsening of symptoms in those with dye sensitivities). Some research and consumer concern links certain artificial colors to behavior changes in susceptible children, though evidence is mixed and effects are not universal. The “lake” form is designed to be more stable in dry or fatty products, and it does not provide nutritional benefit.","category":"Artificial Colorant"}

xylitol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Xylitol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Xylitol is a sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener and is generally safe for most people. It can cause digestive upset in some individuals, especially at higher intakes.","details":"Because it is only partially absorbed, xylitol can draw water into the intestine and be fermented by gut bacteria, leading to gas, bloating, or diarrhea (dose-dependent). It does not raise blood sugar as much as sugar and may help reduce dental cavities. It is extremely toxic to dogs, so caution is needed in households with pets, though this is not a human toxicity concern.","category":"Sugar alcohol sweetener"}

ceramide np__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Ceramide Np","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Ceramide NP is a lipid (fat-like molecule) that supports skin barrier function and is sometimes added to supplements or functional foods. It is generally considered low risk at typical use levels.","details":"Dietary ceramides are often sourced from plants (such as wheat, rice, or konjac) or produced via fermentation, and amounts in products are usually small. Human data suggest it may help with skin hydration and barrier integrity, though results vary by dose and formulation. People with specific ingredient sensitivities should check the source material, but for the general population it is considered low concern.","category":"Skin-support lipid (ceramide)"}

water__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Water","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Water is a common base ingredient in foods and beverages and is generally safe. It is used to dissolve, dilute, or carry other ingredients.","details":"In most products, water functions as the main solvent and helps with texture and consistency. Safety concerns are mainly related to overall product hygiene and quality control rather than water itself. It does not add calories, sugar, or sodium on its own.","category":"Solvent / Base"}

glycerin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Glycerin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Glycerin (glycerol) is commonly used in foods and supplements as a humectant and sweet-tasting texture agent. It is generally considered safe at typical amounts found in products.","details":"It helps retain moisture, prevents drying, and can improve mouthfeel in items like gummies, syrups, and chewables. Glycerin provides calories and has a mild sweet taste, but it does not behave like added sugar in the same way. Large amounts may cause digestive discomfort (such as bloating or diarrhea), especially in sensitive individuals.","category":"Humectant / Sweetener / Texture agent"}

olive fruit oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Olive Fruit Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Olive fruit oil is an edible plant oil rich in monounsaturated fats and is widely used in foods. It is generally considered a health-supportive fat when used in place of saturated fats.","details":"It can provide flavor and contribute to texture, and it contains antioxidant compounds (polyphenols) depending on processing and quality. Like all oils, it is calorie-dense, so overall intake matters for weight and calorie goals. Quality can vary, but typical food-grade olive oil is safe for the general population.","category":"Edible oil / Fat source"}

betaine__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Betaine","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Betaine is a naturally occurring compound found in foods like beets and whole grains and is often used in supplements for methylation and homocysteine support. It is generally considered low risk at typical food and supplement amounts.","details":"In foods, betaine contributes to normal cellular hydration and acts as a methyl donor in metabolism. Supplemental doses can sometimes cause mild gastrointestinal upset or a fishy body odor in sensitive individuals. Very high supplemental intakes may raise LDL cholesterol in some people, so those with lipid concerns should use higher-dose products cautiously.","category":"Nutrient / Supplement ingredient"}

allantoin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Allantoin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Allantoin is a compound commonly used in cosmetics for soothing effects and may appear in some ingestible products in small amounts. For most people, it is low risk at typical additive levels.","details":"Food exposure is generally limited and amounts, when present, are typically low. Safety concerns are uncommon, but as with many additives, very sensitive individuals could experience mild intolerance. If present in a supplement, it is usually not a primary active ingredient and does not provide major nutritional value.","category":"Food additive / Processing aid"}

trehalose__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Trehalose","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Trehalose is a naturally occurring sugar used as a stabilizer and humectant in foods and supplements. It is generally low risk for the general population.","details":"Trehalose provides calories and can contribute to total sugar intake, which may matter for people managing blood glucose or limiting added sugars. It is digested by the enzyme trehalase; rare individuals with trehalase deficiency may experience gastrointestinal symptoms if they consume larger amounts. In many products it is used to help protect flavors, proteins, or probiotics from moisture and processing stress.","category":"Sweetener / Stabilizer"}

cetearyl alcohol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetearyl Alcohol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetearyl alcohol is a fatty alcohol used mainly to stabilize mixtures and improve texture. It is generally considered low risk at typical food/supplement exposure levels.","details":"Despite the word \"alcohol,\" it is not the same as ethanol and does not have intoxicating effects. In products it functions as an emulsifier/thickener and can help keep oil and water components blended. For most people it is well tolerated, though it could cause mild digestive discomfort if consumed in unusually large amounts.","category":"Emulsifier / Texture agent"}

beeswax__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Beeswax","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Beeswax is a natural wax used as a glazing or coating agent and sometimes as a stabilizer. It is generally low risk for the general population.","details":"In foods and supplements it is commonly used to provide shine, reduce sticking, or act as a protective coating (for example on candies or tablets). It is largely indigestible and typically passes through the body without significant absorption. People with sensitivity to bee-related products may rarely react, but typical use levels are considered safe.","category":"Glazing agent / Coating"}

cetyl ethylhexanoate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetyl Ethylhexanoate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetyl ethylhexanoate is a fatty ester primarily used to improve smoothness and mouthfeel in formulations. It is generally considered low risk at the small amounts likely present in ingestible products.","details":"It functions as an emollient-like texture modifier and can help dissolve or disperse fat-soluble ingredients. In the body, fatty esters are typically broken down into fatty alcohols/acids similar to dietary fats, though data for high-dose intake is limited. Most concerns are about formulation quality and sourcing rather than inherent toxicity at low exposure.","category":"Texture agent / Lipid carrier"}

cyclohexasiloxane__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cyclohexasiloxane","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Cyclohexasiloxane is a silicone fluid primarily used in cosmetics and industrial applications, not typical for foods. Its presence in a food or supplement product would be unusual and raises safety and quality concerns.","details":"Cyclohexasiloxane (often called D6) is a volatile siloxane used as a carrier or slip agent in personal care products; it is not a standard approved food additive in many regions. Because it is not commonly intended for ingestion, it may indicate contamination, packaging migration, or mislabeling. If listed on a food or supplement label, it warrants verification with the manufacturer and checking regulatory compliance for your country.","category":"Silicone compound / Processing contaminant concern"}

polysorbate 60__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Polysorbate 60","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Polysorbate 60 is an emulsifier used to keep ingredients mixed and improve texture. It is generally permitted in foods within regulated limits, but some people prefer to limit emulsifiers in heavily processed products.","details":"It helps stabilize mixtures of oil and water in items like baked goods, dessert toppings, and drink mixes, and is typically used at low levels. Some research suggests certain emulsifiers may affect gut barrier function or microbiome in susceptible individuals, though evidence in humans is not definitive and depends on dose and overall diet. If you experience digestive sensitivity, minimizing frequent intake of emulsifier-heavy ultra-processed foods may be reasonable.","category":"Emulsifier / Stabilizer"}

stearic acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Stearic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Stearic acid is a common fatty acid found naturally in foods and also used as a processing aid. In supplements, it is often used as a lubricant to help manufacturing.","details":"It occurs naturally in animal fats and cocoa butter and is widely used in foods and dietary supplements in small amounts. In tablet and capsule production, it helps prevent ingredients from sticking to equipment and can improve consistency. For most people, typical dietary and supplemental exposures are considered safe.","category":"Fatty acid / Processing aid"}

butylene glycol__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Butylene Glycol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Butylene glycol is a synthetic humectant and solvent commonly used in cosmetics and sometimes present in flavored supplements or liquid products as a carrier. In foods it is uncommon, and its presence may indicate a non-traditional additive use.","details":"When used topically it is generally considered low concern, but ingestion use is less typical, so product labeling and regulatory compliance matter. egg__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Egg","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Egg is a nutrient-dense whole food and a common allergen, but it is generally safe for the general population.","details":"Eggs provide high-quality protein and nutrients such as choline, selenium, and B vitamins. agave syrup__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Agave Syrup","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Agave syrup is a sweetener that is often high in fructose, which can be a concern when consumed frequently or in large amounts.","details":"Like other added sugars, agave syrup can contribute to excess calorie intake and dental caries. cottonseed oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cottonseed Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Cottonseed oil is a vegetable oil used for frying and in processed foods. egg whites__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Egg Whites","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Egg whites are a high-quality protein source commonly used in foods and supplements.
